title: Creative About me references
request: Owner request (2026-10-10): redesign the homepage About (קצת עליי) section, using the portrait from the בואו נדבר button and the supplied three-paragraph biography with its bold phrases kept; research inspiration for a creative About section, then build the strongest direction as a local trial.
method: Element pages captured headlessly in Chrome at 1440×900 on 2026-10-10 and visually inspected; Mobbin section previews downloaded from Mobbin. Some captures still show a cookie notice. Awwwards entries are video previews of a single element, so each description covers the captured frame and the element's stated tags, not a full-site audit. Descriptions paraphrase; takeaways are design judgments. The 20 classic layouts in the baseline report are not repeated.

recommendation.name: קשב — the bio demonstrates the method it describes
recommendation.summary: Scroll moves the reading focus through the three paragraphs, and each of the owner’s bold phrases receives a yellow highlighter stroke as it is read. The portrait cutout from the contact button sits on the brand-yellow shape and stays beside the text on desktop.
why: The copy claims methods from attention retention, gradual journeys and smart content division; the section shows them on her own words instead of describing them.
The owner’s bold phrases already mark what matters, so the interaction adds emphasis without new content or invented claims.

Text is never hidden: unfocused paragraphs keep at least 4.5:1 on the canvas (the large bold phrases at least 3:1 over the marker), and without JavaScript or with reduced motion every phrase is drawn.
One signature interaction, matching the owner’s ‘bold but readable’ choice; the yellow ties to the header avatar and the brand secondary colour.

alternatives.name: Portrait mask reveal
alternatives.note: The portrait opens from the yellow shape as the section enters (Sirnik-style reveal applied to the image). More cinematic, but it spends the interaction on the image rather than the message, and the current 600px portrait limits its scale.

alternatives.name: Clickable personal items
alternatives.note: The owner’s backlog idea (2026-10-09). Deferred by the owner on 2026-10-10 until items and meanings are supplied; the layout leaves room beside the portrait.

examples.name: Sol (XKM Studio)
examples.label: Scroll-based text highlight
examples.observed: A long paragraph sits over a dark atmospheric portrait; words already read stay dim while the current sentence turns fully white. Tagged GSAP, scroll, highlight.
examples.takeaway: Progressive emphasis turns reading into the interaction itself.
examples.fit: Primary mechanism reference. Moriz keeps every word readable and highlights only the owner’s bold phrases.

examples.name: Eduard Bodak — Portfolio
examples.label: Highlight benefit on scroll
examples.observed: A ruled list of benefits on black; the row at the reading line brightens while the others remain grey.
examples.takeaway: A single active item at the eye line is enough focus; the rest can stay quietly legible.
examples.fit: Reference for paragraph-level focus on desktop.

examples.name: Sirnik
examples.label: About section with text reveal
examples.observed: A studio statement in large sans type on black, revealed line by line on scroll. Tagged scroll animation, text reveal, minimal.
examples.takeaway: A studio-voice paragraph can carry an About section on typography and motion alone.
examples.fit: Supports a large reading size; the reveal itself is not used, so text never waits to appear.

examples.name: Nephew Media
examples.label: Highlight text on scroll (Webflow clone)
examples.observed: Large grey paragraphs on black; the line at the centre of the viewport lights up as it is reached.
examples.takeaway: Tie the effect to the viewport centre so it follows the visitor’s own pace.
examples.fit: Confirms the eye-line trigger used for the focus calculation.

examples.name: Scroll Reveal Words (Zeroqode)
examples.label: Sticky word highlight band
examples.observed: A sticky band where the current word lights up while the list scrolls past dimmed; includes a screen-reader fallback.
examples.takeaway: Keep the full text available to assistive technology regardless of the visual state.
examples.fit: Accessibility reference; the Moriz text is ordinary DOM text in every state.

examples.name: Regina Musi
examples.label: Editorial About me with numbered facts
examples.observed: A large serif ‘About me’ heading, three numbered short statements (love, past experience, approach) and a black-and-white photograph framed by landscape.
examples.takeaway: Short structured statements plus one honest photograph read as confident and personal.
examples.fit: Typographic confidence reference; Moriz keeps the owner’s continuous paragraphs.

examples.name: Dongkyu Lee
examples.label: About as an interactive card
examples.observed: A calm card with columns (‘Hello, I’m Dongkyu’, ‘I design’, ‘Let’s connect’); secondary content fades in on interaction. Tagged interaction, transition, microinteraction.
examples.takeaway: Microinteractions can stay small and still feel crafted.
examples.fit: Restraint reference: one interaction, done carefully.

examples.name: Freshman
examples.label: Oversized name + small black-and-white portrait
examples.observed: A huge mixed sans/serif name, one short line of positioning, and a small monochrome portrait below.
examples.takeaway: A modest black-and-white portrait works when the typography carries the scale.
examples.fit: Supports keeping the 600px monochrome cutout at a moderate size.

examples.name: Savor
examples.label: Large heading offset against a compact paragraph
examples.observed: A large serif ‘Who we are’ set against a narrow paragraph, with candid photographs below.
examples.takeaway: Asymmetry between heading, text and image gives a restrained section presence.
examples.fit: Composition reference for the two-column split.

baselineReferences.name: Dennis Snellenberg
baselineReferences.use: Asymmetric portrait composition with a short client-facing paragraph.

baselineReferences.name: Adham Dannaway
baselineReferences.use: Cutout portrait beside a compact bio.

baselineReferences.name: Seán Halpin
baselineReferences.use: Distinctive portrait shape that makes the section feel warm.
